_README: Classified divergences for ci/fixture_ab.sh - both engines against RVF's own
regression fixture, per assertion, in about 45 seconds.
Its own file because the fixture is not a release. A cause proven on 58 files
of deliberately broken 2013 test data transfers nowhere else. This arm also
loads ci/known-engine-divergences.json, whose entries are engine defects
rather than release facts, and which therefore do apply here.
STATE 2026-09-10, all three SQL groups: 210 assertions joined, 209 identical
(99.5%), 1 divergent - the entry below. MySQL 159 failures, DuckDB 158.
THE FIVE RAGGED-ROW ENTRIES ARE GONE, and how they went is the point of this
arm. They were 20 malformed rows across both fixtures: a TAB inside three
terms (splitting one field into two), sixteen rows missing caseSignificanceId
entirely, and one association row with a double tab leaving an empty field.
The tab sat at a DIFFERENT position in Delta than in Snapshot for the same
description id, which is what proved it was corruption and not a designed
case - no test case differs per file. Repairing them took this arm from 5
divergences to 0 on release-type-validation, and moved seven DuckDB
assertions' findings DOWN to MySQL's numbers: DuckDB had been reporting
findings about the corruption itself.
WHY THE PACKAGE IS REPACKED AS CRLF: RF2 files are CRLF and RVF's MySQL
loader says so - `lines terminated by '\r\n' ignore 1 lines`. The fixture is
LF-only, so that statement read each file as ONE line, discarded it, and
loaded 0 rows with no error: 90 empty tables and every previous-dependent
assertion passing over nothing. Before that normalisation this arm read 50.9%
identical and every MySQL number in it was meaningless.

2e0eb135-fd7d-4f24-83c1-0cba797ee766.appliesTo: component-centric-snapshot-description-unique-term-in-concept, and ~20 other assertions that join or group on term
2e0eb135-fd7d-4f24-83c1-0cba797ee766.observed: MySQL 1 in assertionsFailed; DuckDB 0 in assertionsPassed
cause: MySQL IS RIGHT AND THIS IS A DUCKDB FALSE NEGATIVE. It is listed so the
gate stays usable, NOT because the answer is acceptable.
Concept 703860006 has two ACTIVE descriptions whose terms differ only in
trailing whitespace:
2989790014  active=1  term='Exposure to vibration  '   (two trailing)
2989790017  active=1  term='Exposure to vibration '    (one trailing)
MySQL's collation is PAD SPACE: trailing spaces are ignored in comparison
and in GROUP BY, so the two rows group together, count(distinct id) is 2,
and the duplicate is reported. DuckDB compares exactly, sees two distinct
terms, and reports nothing.
The assertion is 'For a given concept, all active description terms are
unique', and its own comment says so. Two terms differing only by trailing
spaces are indistinguishable to a reader and violate that. The port is
otherwise faithful - source and transpiled SQL both filter active = 1 and
both use count(distinct a.id) > 1 - so this is not a transpilation slip in
this assertion, it is a string-semantics difference the port does not yet
model.
EXPOSURE, measured across the bundled corpus: 21 statements in 19
assertions join term = term, 8 statements in 8 assertions GROUP BY term,
and 1 uses DISTINCT over term. Only this one fires on this fixture because
only this concept has a trailing-space duplicate; the other ~20 are latent.
This is the same SHAPE as the REGEXP work: a MySQL string behaviour that
has to be replicated deliberately rather than assumed. See
duck/REGEXP-PARITY.md for how that one was measured and closed.
evidence: MySQL report detail: 'Duplicate term=Exposure to vibration  '
Loading the same file by hand and running MySQL's own query returns no rows,
which is what pointed at the collation rather than the data
2e0eb135-fd7d-4f24-83c1-0cba797ee766.moveWhen: The port normalises trailing whitespace where MySQL's PAD SPACE collation would, and both engines report 1
